text: the 25% reduction in carbon emissions for this 2024 fuel mix projection with a focus strictly on Scope 1 analysis (energy use on site) can be done by two scenarios as follows: • Scenario 1: Integration of Zero Carbon Fuel in Natural Gas Mix • Scenario 2: Increasing Biomass Utilization to Reduce Natural Gas Consumption For Scenario 1, we maintain the following conditions: • Avoid changes to biomass boiler • Adjust carbon profile of natural gas (NG) power boiler • Assume 83% efficiency for NG boiler 55 DE-EE0009395 • Determine blend of fossil-fuel NG and carbon-free fuel (e.g., renewable natural gas or hydrogen) In this scenario, the mix of natural gas in power boilers is altered from 33% to a combination of 24% natural gas and 9% carbon-free fuel, resulting in a reduction of CO emissions from 117 to 2 87 lb/MMBtu to meet the 25% carbon reduction target. The contribution of fuel from biomass remains consistent at 67%. The breakdown of the fuel mix and carbon emissions can be observed in Figure 42a-d and Table 16 respectively. For Scenario 2, the following conditions are considered: • Introduce additional biomass • Reduce natural gas contribution to power boiler • Assume 67% efficiency for biomass boiler • Determine increase of biomass utilization to fossil-fuel NG and carbon-free biomass In this scenario, the fuel mix shifts, with biomass utilization rising from 67% to 76%, while natural gas decreases from 33% to 24%, as illustrated in Figure 42a-d. In effect, this second scenario accomplishes the same effect as the first scenario in shifting 9 percentage points of carbon- containing natural gas to a carbon free fuel. In Scenario 1, it could have been a fuel such as hydrogen. In Scenario 2, it is increased use of biomass. The outcomes for both scenarios are outlined in Table 16, which serves as a reference for the baseline carbon footprint associated with the utilization of steam derived from natural gas and biomass.
